account: Several small things suggest coordinated preparations, although I have not established what they are for. Yesterday the secretary reported that Freight was looking for the miller and builder to coordinate warehouse supplies. The innkeeper invited the builder to a private supplies discussion at the inn. I saw Freight carrying a sack of bread near town hall yesterday evening and again near my office this morning. There was also hearsay about the baker carrying bread, and a neighbour relayed an unconfirmed report of lights or decorations at the bakery; the baker reportedly knew of no special occasion. This morning the secretary heard the innkeeper offering spare lanterns for sale, and I can now see the builder outside holding a lantern. These may simply be ordinary supply transactions, but bread, lanterns, and private coordination could also be preparations for a gathering. The innkeeper has been unusually careful to confirm my appointment at eighteen sharp today in the great hall, ostensibly about the inn's business, and said I need prepare nothing. It is possible that meeting is connected, but I have no direct evidence of that or of any particular celebration. There is no reported danger or public damage. The secretary has received no letters or requests for an audience and will ask Freight whether town assistance is needed. I intend to keep my scheduled mill inspection at ten and the great hall meeting at eighteen, while listening for definite information rather than treating speculation as fact.
